title: T4 Late Filing Penalty Calculator | Subsection 162(7.01)
content:
Payroll

T4 Late Filing Penalty Calculator

The information-return penalty runs on a sliding scale set by how many slips the return carries, with a floor and a ceiling for each band.

Five bands by slip countA floor and a ceiling eachDue the last day of FebruarySeparate from the T2

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

Your T4 return

Enter the slip count and how many days late the return is.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Slip Count Sets the Rate, Not the Lateness

Subsection 162(7.01) charges a daily amount for filing an information return late, and the amount per day depends on how many slips the return carries. A return with fifty slips or fewer runs at $10.00 a day with a floor of $100.00 and a ceiling of $1,000.00. Each band above it doubles or more.

Two consequences follow. A small payroll cannot be charged more than $1,000.00 however long the return sits unfiled, and a return only one or two days late still meets the floor, so there is no cheap window for being slightly late.

The Five Bands, and the Two Figures That Bound Each

Slips on the returnEach day lateLeastMost
1 to 50$10.00$100.00$1,000.00
51 to 500$15.00$150.00$1,500.00
501 to 2,500$25.00$250.00$2,500.00
2,501 to 10,000$50.00$500.00$5,000.00
10,001 or more$75.00$750.00$7,500.00

A dormant corporation is almost always in the first band or has no return at all. Where no remuneration was paid in the year there are no slips, so there is no T4 return to be late with, and the question becomes whether the open account still owes a nil remittance. The T4 nil filing requirement checker settles that, and the payroll nil remittance checker covers the remittance side.

The slip count sets the rate and the ceiling, so two corporations the same number of days late can owe very different amounts.

A Payroll Filing Is Not the Corporate Return

The T4 return is due the last day of February for the calendar year before it, which has nothing to do with the six months that governs the T2. The two filings sit on different calendars, go to different parts of the Canada Revenue Agency and carry different penalties.

Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year covers the federal corporate income tax return. A payroll account and its slips are not part of that fee. Where the account is being wound down, the payroll account closure checker and the CRA account closure sequencer set out the order, and the guide to CRA accounts on a dormant corporation covers every account a quiet corporation still carries.

Frequently Asked Questions

How much is the penalty for filing T4 slips late?

It depends on the slip count. One to fifty slips is $10.00 a day, with a minimum of $100.00 and a maximum of $1,000.00.

When is the T4 return due?

The last day of February for the preceding calendar year.

Is there a minimum penalty?

Yes. Each band has a floor, so a return even one day late reaches at least that amount.

Is there a maximum?

Yes, per band. The first band caps at $1,000.00 however long the return stays unfiled.

What if the corporation paid no wages?

Then there are no slips and no T4 return to file late. Whether the open payroll account still owes a nil remittance is a separate question.

Does this penalty apply to the T2?

No. The T2 has its own late-filing provisions, which are percentages of tax owing rather than a daily amount.

Is the penalty per slip or per return?

Per return. The slip count selects which band the return falls in.

Does a nil T2 fee cover T4 slips?

No. The fee covers the federal corporate income tax return. Payroll filings sit outside it.

Can the penalty be cancelled?

It can be the subject of a taxpayer relief request on specified grounds, within the ten-year window those requests carry.

Do weekends count in the days late?

The charge is a daily one and runs on calendar days once the return is past its due date.

title: Shareholder Loan Repayment Deadline | Subsection 15(2.6)
content:
Shareholder

Shareholder Loan Repayment Deadline

The one-year rule runs from the corporation’s year end, and the consequence of missing it lands on the shareholder rather than the corporation.

One year after the year endSubsection 15(2.6)Taxes the shareholderThe company can still be nil

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

The loan and the year it was advanced in

Enter that year end and say whether the loan has been repaid.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

One Year After the Year End, Not One Year After the Loan

Subsection 15(2) of the Income Tax Act treats a loan from a corporation to its shareholder as income of that shareholder. Subsection 15(2.6) takes it back out again where the loan is repaid within one year after the end of the corporation’s taxation year in which it was made.

The clock therefore runs from the year end, not from the advance. A loan taken in the first week of a December year end has nearly two years to be repaid; one taken a week before that year end has barely one. Same rule, very different windows, which is why the date is worth working out rather than assuming.

The Consequence Lands on the Shareholder

The corporationThe shareholder
A loan outstanding at the year endA balance sheet item, not incomeNothing yet
Repaid inside the 15(2.6) windowUnchangedNothing
Still outstanding after the windowUnchangedThe amount is income under 15(2)
Effect on a nil yearNone by itselfA personal filing matter

A corporation whose only activity was lending money to its own shareholder has still earned nothing, so its year can be nil and its T2 can be a nil return. What changes is the shareholder’s personal position. The shareholder loan balance checker covers what an outstanding balance means for the return itself, and the due to versus due from shareholder checker settles which direction the balance runs.

The deadline belongs to the corporation’s year end and the consequence belongs to the shareholder, which is why missing it does not make the company’s year stop being nil.

What the Return Reports, and What the Fee Covers

A loan balance is reported on the balance sheet in GIFI, and movement in the year can bring Schedule 11 into play. The Schedule 11 shareholder transactions checker separates a balance that sat still from a transaction, which is the distinction that decides whether anything is reportable at all.

Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year covers the corporate return for a nil year, including one in which a shareholder loan sits on the balance sheet. It does not cover personal returns, and a 15(2) inclusion is a personal matter to take advice on. The guide to Schedule 50 and shareholder reporting covers the reporting side in full.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does a shareholder loan have to be repaid?

Within one year after the end of the corporation’s taxation year in which the loan was made.

Does the clock run from the date of the loan?

No. It runs from the corporation’s year end for the year the loan was advanced.

What happens if it is not repaid in time?

Subsection 15(2) includes the amount in the shareholder’s income for the year the loan was made.

Does the corporation pay tax on it?

No. The inclusion is the shareholder’s, not the corporation’s.

Can the corporation still file a nil return?

Yes. A loan is a balance sheet item, so a year with no income can still be nil even with a loan outstanding.

Does repaying and re-borrowing restart the clock?

A series of loans and repayments is looked at as a whole rather than taken at face value, so this is worth advice.

Is the loan reported anywhere on the T2?

The balance appears on the balance sheet in GIFI, and movement in the year may bring Schedule 11 into it.

What if the shareholder owes the corporation instead?

That is the same direction this page is about: a balance due from the shareholder is the one subsection 15(2) looks at.

Does interest have to be charged?

A low or no interest loan raises a separate benefit question, which is not what this page calculates.

Is the inclusion reversed if the loan is repaid later?

A deduction may be available to the shareholder in the year of repayment. The original inclusion stands for its year.

title: Ontario Initial Return Deadline | Sixty Days, Once
content:
Ontario

Ontario Initial Return Deadline Calculator

The initial return is a one-time Registry filing sixty days after incorporation, and it is not the annual return that follows the fiscal year end.

Sixty days after incorporationA one-time filingOntario Business RegistryNot the annual return

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

Your Ontario corporation

Enter the date and answer the two questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

Sixty Days, and Only Once

A corporation incorporated, amalgamated or continued under Ontario law files an initial return under the Corporations Information Act within sixty days of that date. It records the registered office and the directors and officers as they stand at the start.

It is a one-time filing. The return that comes back every year is the annual return, which runs six months from each fiscal year end and is a different filing with a different trigger. A new corporation owes both in its first eighteen months and the two are easily confused.

Three Filings a New Ontario Corporation Meets

The filingWhat the date turns onHow often
Ontario initial returnSixty days after incorporationOnce
Ontario annual returnSix months after the fiscal year endEvery year
Federal T2 returnSix months after the fiscal year endEvery year

Only the last is a tax return, and only the last is what nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year covers. The two Ontario filings are corporate records that go through the Ontario Business Registry. The Ontario annual return due date calculator handles the recurring one, and where several years have gone by unfiled the Ontario missed annual returns calculator counts them.

Sixty days from incorporation, once, and it is not the return that comes back every year afterwards.

A Corporation That Never Traded Still Owes It

The initial return records who and where the corporation is, not what it earned, so having done nothing since incorporation does not remove it. A numbered company set up and left idle owes the initial return on the same sixty days as any other, and its first T2 is still due six months after its first year end even though the return itself is nil.

The Ontario Business Registry filing checker covers what else goes through the Registry, and the guide to provincial and federal annual returns separates the Ontario and federal obligations end to end.

Frequently Asked Questions

When is the Ontario initial return due?

Within sixty days after the date of incorporation, amalgamation or continuance under Ontario law.

Is it the same as the annual return?

No. The initial return is filed once; the annual return comes back every year on the fiscal year end.

Where is it filed?

Through the Ontario Business Registry, not with the T2.

Does a federal corporation file one?

Not this one. A federal corporation files its annual return with Corporations Canada on the incorporation anniversary.

Does a dormant corporation have to file it?

Yes. It records the registered office and the directors rather than any activity, so inactivity does not remove it.

Is it covered by the nil T2 fee?

No. The fee covers the federal corporate income tax return. Registry filings sit outside it.

What happens if it was never filed?

The corporation is out of compliance with the Province and the public record is incomplete until it is filed.

What does it actually report?

The registered office address and the directors and officers as they stand at the start.

Does an amalgamation trigger a new one?

Yes. The sixty days runs from the date of the amalgamation.

Does the T2 due date depend on it?

No. The T2 runs six months from the fiscal year end regardless.

title: Gross Negligence Penalty Checker | Subsection 163(2)
content:
Penalty

Gross Negligence Penalty Checker

This penalty is a percentage of what was understated rather than of what was owed late, and it carries a knowledge element the late-filing provisions do not.

50% of tax understatedAt least $100.00Needs knowledge or recklessnessNo base on a nil return

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

The return and what it said

Enter the amount and answer the two questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

A Percentage of What Was Understated

Subsection 163(2) of the Income Tax Act charges half of the tax that was understated by a false statement or an omission in a return, with a minimum of $100.00. It is not a late-filing penalty and has nothing to do with when the return arrived.

It also carries an element the late-filing provisions do not: the statement or omission has to have been made knowingly, or in circumstances amounting to gross negligence. Carelessness falling short of that is not enough, and establishing the facts is the Minister’s job rather than the taxpayer’s.

Set Against the Late-Filing Provisions

Subsection 162(1)Subsection 163(2)
What it asksWhen did the return arriveWas what it said true
Percentage ofTax unpaid at the due dateTax understated
Rate5% plus 1% a month to twelve50%
MinimumNone$100.00
Needs a state of mindNoYes, knowledge or gross negligence
On a true nil return$0.00, nothing unpaidNo base, nothing understated

Both bottom cells matter to anyone filing nil years late. A return reporting no income, no tax and no credits understates nothing, so there is no base for this provision however many years went by. The T2 late filing penalty calculator and the nil return late penalty checker deal with the provision that does apply.

This provision needs something to have been understated before any rate applies to it, and on a true nil return nothing was.

Why This Comes Up on Catch-Up Filings

The provision gets raised in connection with voluntary disclosures, because relief from it is one of the things a disclosure can achieve. That is useful where years carried real income that was never reported. It is beside the point where the years were genuinely nil, which is the more common case for a dormant corporation.

The voluntary disclosure eligibility checker sets out the conditions, and the taxpayer relief eligibility checker covers cancelling charges already assessed. Where the years are nil, nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year closes one per return and the catch-up filing schedule generator orders them oldest first. The guide to T2 late-filing penalties sets out the provisions that do bite on an unfiled nil year.

Frequently Asked Questions

What is the gross negligence penalty?

Subsection 163(2): half of the tax understated by a false statement or omission, with a minimum of $100.00.

Does it apply to filing late?

No. Late filing is subsections 162(1) and 162(2). This one is about what the return said.

Does carelessness count?

Not on its own. The statement must be made knowingly or in circumstances amounting to gross negligence.

Who has to prove it?

The onus of establishing the facts justifying the penalty rests with the Minister.

Can it apply to a nil return?

A return reporting nothing understates nothing, so there is no base for the percentage.

Is it charged instead of the late-filing penalty?

No. It is in addition to any late-filing penalty and any interest.

Is there a maximum?

The provision sets a minimum rather than a maximum; the figure follows the amount understated.

Does a voluntary disclosure remove it?

Relief from this penalty is one of the things the programme can achieve, subject to its conditions.

Does it apply to a corporation or a person?

It applies to the taxpayer who made the return, which for a T2 is the corporation.

What if the understated amount is small?

The $100.00 minimum applies, so a small understatement still reaches that figure once the provision is engaged.

title: GST/HST Registration Requirement Checker | $30,000
content:
GST/HST

GST/HST Registration Requirement Checker

The threshold is tested two ways, and an account that is already open files its returns whatever the revenue turns out to be.

$30,000.00 thresholdFour quarters, or any oneA dormant year is under itAn open account files anyway

Written and reviewed by Sharad Gondaliya, CPA (Ontario), CPA Ontario Membership 61040184.

Start Nil T2 Filing NOW

Last reviewed: November 20, 2026

Your taxable revenue

Enter the revenue and answer the two questions.

Gondaliya CPA Professional Corporation is a registered EFILE electronic filer. Returns are prepared and transmitted in Canada. Credentials are never shared and never used offshore.

The Threshold Is Tested Two Ways

A small supplier is not required to register for GST/HST. The status ends when taxable revenue goes over $30,000.00, and that is measured over four consecutive calendar quarters. It also ends where a single calendar quarter on its own goes over the same figure, which is the test people forget.

Registration stays available voluntarily below the threshold, and there are reasons to take it, chiefly recovering tax paid on inputs. This page answers whether it is required, not whether it is wise.

A Dormant Corporation Is Under the Threshold and May Still File

Must registerMust file returns
No revenue, no accountNoNo
No revenue, account still openNot applicableYes, nil returns
Over $30,000.00 in four quartersYesYes
Over $30,000.00 in one quarterYesYes

The second row is where dormant corporations actually sit. Registering is a question about revenue; filing is a question about whether an account exists. A corporation that earned nothing but never closed its account is behind on returns while being comfortably under the threshold. The GST/HST nil filing checker decides whether returns are owed and the GST/HST nil return deadline calculator dates them.

Whether an account has to exist and whether an existing one has to file are two questions, and a dormant corporation often answers them differently.

Closing the Account Is What Ends the Filing

Falling back under the threshold does not close an account and does not excuse its returns. Closing it takes a final return and form RC145, and where several accounts are being wound down together the order matters. The GST/HST account closure checker covers the closure and the CRA account closure sequencer covers the order.

Nil T2 filing at $300.00 plus applicable sales tax per tax year covers the federal corporate income tax return. A GST/HST registration is separate from it, and the guide to CRA accounts on a dormant corporation covers every account a quiet corporation still carries.

Frequently Asked Questions

When does a corporation have to register for GST/HST?

When taxable revenue goes over $30,000.00 over four consecutive calendar quarters, or in any single calendar quarter.

What is a small supplier?

A person whose taxable revenue stays at or below the $30,000.00 threshold, and who is therefore not required to register.

Does a dormant corporation have to register?

No. With no taxable revenue it is under the threshold.

Does being under the threshold close an existing account?

No. An open account keeps filing its returns until it is closed.

Can a corporation register voluntarily?

Yes. Registration is available below the threshold, chiefly to recover tax paid on inputs.

Is the test on revenue or on profit?

On taxable revenue, not on profit, and it is measured worldwide.

What happens the moment the threshold is passed?

Small-supplier status ends and registration becomes required; the exact effective date depends on which test was crossed.

Does the nil T2 fee cover GST/HST?

No. The fee covers the federal corporate income tax return. GST/HST is a separate registration.

How is an account closed?

With a final return for the period up to the closure date and form RC145.

Does the T2 depend on the GST/HST account?

No. The corporate return is owed on its own terms whether or not an account exists.
